passage: Thabo's phone said 3:07 again. In Johannesburg the house was silent and he was awake, scrolling. At lunch that day, Yara had asked how he got through the week on so little sleep, and Thabo realised he had never asked himself why. That night he drew three columns: when I really go to bed, what I do from six to ten, what I do after. The answers were plain. From six to ten he watched videos and called it resting. He started studying at ten, when guilt kicked in. After a stressful day he scrolled to switch his head off, until three. The day had enough hours; he was spending the best ones on avoiding. At the bottom of the page he wrote: "Study six to eight. Phone off the bed."

qa.q: What time did Thabo's phone show?
What did Thabo realise about the late nights?
qa.a: Thabo realised that he was spending the early evening on videos and starting to study late out of guilt, then scrolling after a stressful day.

qa.q: What other step could Thabo try, and why?
qa.a: Thabo could do a short walk or talk to Yara after a stressful day instead of scrolling, because it lets the head wind down without eating into the night.

qa.q: How might Yara see Thabo's tiredness?
qa.a: Yara probably worries and wonders how Thabo copes, having asked at lunch how he gets through the week on so little sleep.

grounding: A student sleeping at 3 am asks why, and finds it comes from late-night scrolling after a stressful day and studying during the evening's wasted hours, not from a lack of hours in the day.

passage:
In the hostel common room, Imran slumped over his physics book at 7 pm, already yawning. His roommate Hrithik looked up from the carrom board. "You slept at three again?"

"I don't have enough hours," Imran said. "Coaching, school, homework."

"Do you, though?" Hrithik asked. "Write down yesterday."

Imran pulled a notebook toward him, thinking aloud. "Back from coaching at six. Then I lay on the bed with my phone because the day was awful. Suddenly it's nine. Dinner. Then I start homework at ten, get tired, scroll again. Then I study from one to three because I panic."

He stared at the page. "So from six to nine, I did nothing. That's three hours."

"And the scrolling after a bad day," Hrithik said.

Imran underlined it twice. "It's not the hours. It's what I do with them."

qa.q: What time did Imran come back from coaching?
qa.a: He came back from coaching at six.

qa.q: How did Imran feel when he saw the three empty hours on the page?
qa.a: Imran felt surprised and a little embarrassed, realising the problem was his evening habits, not a lack of hours.

qa.q: What could Imran try first, now that he sees the pattern?
qa.a: He could do a short, planned break after coaching and start homework by seven, so the stressful day doesn't turn into three hours of scrolling.

qa.q: How might Hrithik see Imran's discovery?
qa.a: Hrithik probably feels pleased and a bit relieved, having nudged Imran to look at the actual day instead of just complaining about hours.

grounding: Shows a student asking why he sleeps at 3 am and finding it comes from scrolling after a stressful day and wasted evening hours, not a lack of time.

passage:
Dear Harsha,

You asked why I've been less of a zombie lately. I'll tell you, because you're up at 3 am too, I've seen your messages.

For months I thought I just didn't have enough hours. So one Sunday I wrote down every single thing I did from 4 pm to bedtime the previous day. It was embarrassing.

4 to 5: tuition. 5 to 8: phone. Not relaxing, just scrolling, because school had been awful and I didn't want to think. 8 to 9: dinner and TV. 9 to 11: slow homework. 11 to 3: panicking, studying, scrolling in between.

That's three hours of phone after a bad day. The hours were there. I was just spending them on hiding.

I'm trying to study from 5 now, with the phone in the kitchen. It's hard, but I slept at midnight twice this week.

Pranav

qa.q: What did Pranav do from 5 to 8?
qa.a: Pranav was on the phone, just scrolling, because school had been awful.

qa.q: How did Pranav feel writing down the whole evening?
qa.a: Pranav felt embarrassed seeing it on paper, and a bit relieved to finally understand the cause.

qa.q: What else could Pranav try if studying from 5 feels too hard?
qa.a: Pranav could take a short, timed break after tuition, like a walk, so the stressful day is let go without three hours of scrolling.

qa.q: How might Harsha feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Harsha might feel understood and a little hopeful, since Pranav admits the same 3 am habit and shows a way to look at it.

grounding: A letter shows a student tracing late nights to scrolling after a stressful day and wasted evening hours rather than a real lack of time.
